results.text: Applying the vulnerability approach to the World Bank’s harmonized household surveys—estimating, for each economy, the probability that a household is living on less than the poverty line of the relevant income group over a few years, and identifying the consumption level at which this probability becomes low—yields economic security lines of about $6.00, $7.00, and $14.00 a day for the three income groups. This is roughly twice the corresponding poverty lines, but with wide variation across economies (Bolch et al. 2026). The threshold also shifts with the risks households face. In Europe and Central Asia, the income needed to maintain a low probability of falling into poverty rose by about 10 percent in real terms between 2008 and 2018 as the shocks pushing households into poverty grew larger (Bussolo et al. 2025).
